problem_text:
A logistics firm must coordinate a surveillance drone to inspect eight critical communication hubs positioned across a region. The geographic coordinates of each hub, measured in relative grid units, are as follows:

Hub P: (33,10)
Hub Q: (76,3)
Hub R: (194,114)
Hub S: (84,41)
Hub T: (38,167)
Hub U: (117,95)
Hub V: (129,97)
Hub W: (135,128)

The flight path distances between hubs, in kilometers, are precomputed:
P to R: 191.7 km
P to S: 59.7 km
P to T: 157.1 km
P to U: 119.5 km
P to V: 129.6 km
P to W: 156.0 km
Q to R: 162.0 km
Q to S: 38.8 km
Q to T: 168.3 km
Q to U: 100.7 km
Q to V: 107.9 km
Q to W: 138.2 km
R to S: 132.0 km
R to T: 164.8 km
R to U: 79.3 km
R to V: 67.2 km
R to W: 60.6 km
S to T: 134.1 km
S to U: 63.3 km
S to V: 71.8 km
S to W: 100.8 km
T to U: 106.9 km
T to V: 114.8 km
T to W: 104.5 km
U to V: 12.2 km
U to W: 37.6 km
V to W: 31.6 km

Due to a permanent signal interference zone, a direct flight between Hub P and Hub Q is impossible. Furthermore, operational protocols mandate that exactly one of two designated secure corridors must be incorporated into the inspection circuit: either the link between Hub Q and Hub R, or the link between Hub R and Hub S.

The objective is to determine the minimal total flight distance for a closed-circuit route that inspects each hub precisely one time, commencing and concluding at the same hub.
